# Milestone order

**ID:** `mandate.milestone-order`
**Status:** `mandate`
**Depends on:** `mandate.baseline`

Work proceeds in this order: M1 parity, M2 adopted interaction changes, M3
succession and full score lifecycle, then M4 universal coarse world
composition, channel-specific providers, rich regional promotion, and broader
content. Later runway types and non-selectable candidates may land earlier for
compatibility or planning, but their existence is not acceptance of M4.

M1 is the complete one-way Rust and Godot replacement of the pinned executable behavior: validate, freeze, run with transcript and endogeneity output, replay checking, interactive play and its twelve verbs, three policy packages, 86 retained tests, and ten gates. It adds fail-closed content compilation, static handler registration, generated fidelity permissions, deterministic replay, and exact checkpoint/resume. Python leaves production after parity.

M2 adds the named chief of staff, visible calendar with discretionary periods and dated capacity, folder handoff, authored speaking commitments, typed commands and immutable projections, practical cards, interruptions, evidence-bounded requests, and a separate extradiegetic scorecard beside in-world review.

M3 implements campaign continuity across Chair succession, chairmanship and
campaign dossiers, full immutable Stewardship findings and adjustments, and
the terminal review rule. M4 initializes every sovereign in each dated world
profile through a typed coarse component bundle; implements recorded and
responsive provider channels, deterministic rich-to-coarse reconciliation,
supported transition closure, UTC and local-calendar composition, feasible
project envelopes, approved asset pipeline coverage, and broader world content.
